page0.text:
Let's go talk to Saber.
...Even if we defeat Gilgamesh, Saber will still be gone once this fight is over.
Saber will destroy the Holy Grail with her own hands, and release herself from her duty as a Servant.
When that moment comes, I won't be able to see her anymore.

page1.text:
...This will be our last conversation.
Before we head into our last battle, I want to make sure we've left something tangible behind for the two of us.

page2.text:
"Shirou? Did something happen to make you come here?"
"Well, nothing really happened. I just wanted to see your face. Oh, I'm sorry if I'm interfering with something. Maybe you were trying to concentrate before the big fight."

page3.text:
"What... N-no, nothing of the sort.
I also wanted to see your face, so I am happy that you are here... Umm, I thought you would've gone to Rin's room for sure."

page4.text: "Hmmm? Why would I go to Tohsaka's room? It's not like she called me to her room or anything."

page5.text:
"Y-you are right. It seems that my assumption was off, please forget about what I said.
M-maybe it was unnecessary, but I-I just thought maybe that would be for the best...or something like that."

page6.text:
"...?"
Saber is acting even more weird.
...Not sure why, but I feel like her face will get infinitely redder if I leave her be, so I decide to ask:

page7.text:
"What's wrong, Saber? You're acting weird right now.
Did something happen?"

page8.text:
"N-nothing weird happened. I-I was simply trying to rest up and get ready for the fight ahead of us.
I could ask you the same thing. Are you not planning to sleep for a bit and be in the best possible condition before we head to Ryudou Temple?"

page9.text:
"Mrgh."
When she puts it like that, it's really hard to say directly to her face that I just wanted to spend time with her.

page10.text:
If I can't say that...
"Ummm, I can't really sleep. So I was thinking if I'm up already, I might as well come here and get a cup of tea with you.
I mean Tohsaka seems kind of busy anyway."
I didn't really think too much and just told her how I felt.

page11.text: "Tea...you say? When we are about to go face the King of Heroes in just a few hours?"

page12.text:
"Yeah. I figure we're probably both too tense to properly rest.
Then spend some time with me, Saber. I will treat you to the best tea I have."

page13.text: "You're right. I would be glad to spend time with you, Shirou."

page14.text:
...Then we must strike the iron while it's hot.
I head back to the kitchen to brew a pot of the Chinese tea that I bought just for this occasion, thinking I will treat Saber to it.

page15.text:
Then...
In the end, we enjoyed the tea together, and nothing else happened.
We didn't strike up a conversation, not even a short exchange of phrases.
We simply sat there and stared at the dojo.
It was a short few days, but we've exchanged quality time here... I think this while staring at the wooden floor.

page16.text:
"Shirou, you should go find Rin. Knowing her, she's probably already come up with something new."
"Yeah, maybe. I will go if you say so."
I stand up and leave the dojo.

page17.text:
"Well then, Shirou, see you soon."
"Yeah. Let me go check up on that angry Master of yours."

page18.text:
I leave the dojo as Saber says goodbye to me.
...In the end, that was our last time spent together.
Nothing tangible was left behind between us.
There were neither promises nor warmth that would sear into my memory. I couldn't create a single sign to remind me that Saber was indeed here.

page19.text:
...But, I have a feeling perhaps that's for the best.
Whatever's left behind will eventually end up being a fading memory.
That's why I'll make sure I keep the memories of the simple times we've spent together close to my heart...

page20.text:
"Heeey, Tohsaka. Are you awake?"
I knock on her door.

page21.text: "...I am awake. What about you? You don't need to sleep? It looks like you were spending some quality time with Saber at the dojo."

page22.text:
"Oh? I didn't know you were watching us.
...That makes sense, though. You could see the dojo clearly from your room.
In that case, you should've come down to the dojo. If you were awake, the three of us could've had some tea together."

page23.text:
"...Whatever.
...I really didn't think that would work out.
Anyway, just come in. I was just thinking about going to find you guys to talk about something."
Hmmm. She seems kinda irritated at something.

page24.text:
"...Got it, thanks."
Still wondering what she's thinking, I enter the room and slowly close the door behind me.

page25.text:
"Aren't you confident? What were you doing with Saber?"
Whoa.
She glares at me as soon as we see each other.

page26.text:
"Nothing really. We were just drinking tea.
We have a big battle coming up, so we wouldn't be sparring. I can't just waste my energy, after all."

page27.text:
"Waste your energy... O-of course, you really can't afford to waste your energy."
...Huh?
Why did you get quiet all of a sudden?

page28.text:
"Tohsaka, are you in a really bad mood right now?"
I already know what she's going to say, but it doesn't hurt to ask.
"WHAT DO YOU THINK?"
She'd obviously yell at me, but I really am curious, so I end up asking her anyway.
However...

page29.text:
"...Never mind. It's not like I'm actually mad at you."
Well, now she's making me even more confused.

page30.text:
"Tohsaka, do you...have a fever or something?"
"No, I don't! ...Ugh, will you just sit down already!?
I will think of something to deal with Gilgamesh since you can't think of anything by yourself!"

page31.text:
Tohsaka drags me inside the room and locks the door. Then she slowly moves back into the room.
"...?"
Anyway, I start to move toward the center of the room.
Facing toward Tohsaka, I sit down across from her.

page32.text:
...
...
And somehow we're both not saying a word, this feels awkward...

page33.text:
"Tohsaka, about Gilgamesh..."
"...I know. You're going to tell me you don't want to have Saber fight him, right? You're really considerate of her."

page34.text:
"Hold on, that's not what I'm talking about.
I'm simply saying that Gilgamesh is a bad match for Saber, so we should rethink our formation, that's all. If Saber is defeated and no one is left to slow him down, Tohsaka would be next."

page35.text:
"...I see. Well how do you propose we change our formation?
I'm not going up against that Goldy. He is taking advantage of his treasury and has anti-magecraft armor on. He's a bad match for Saber but an even worse match for me. Same for you."

page37.text:
...But I just can't forget those eyes.
What Archer's gaze was trying to tell me.
That golden Servant.
Only Shirou Emiya can go up against Gilgamesh.
